symptom: The comprehensive public QA reported every mobile results map as missing and several loaded maps as absent or unclickable.
expected_behavior: The QA must verify first-visit privacy state, then recognize the live map DOM and click a pointer-accessible marker without confusing an overlay or cluster with a broken map.
environment: Public VII production at https://vii.spaplus.co on 2026-10-24, Chromium desktop, 390x844 mobile and 390x620 low-height viewports.

steps: Open a fresh mobile results page without a stored cookie choice.
Scroll the results region and inspect the map control.
Choose essential-only privacy, open the map and inspect map tiles and markers.
Compare the rendered map DOM with the selectors and click target used by the QA.
reproduction.evidence: Before consent the map control existed but display was none because the visible privacy card intentionally occupied the fixed control area. After essential-only consent it was visible. A loaded vacation map exposed 25 tiles and 7 markers while the QA's obsolete .leaflet-container selector matched zero nodes.

observations.observation: The product intentionally suppresses the fixed mobile map button while the cookie card is displayed.
observations.evidence: Computed style was display:none with a present .cookie-card; after localStorage vii-cookie-choice=essential, the same button was display:flex and visible.

observations.observation: The live map may render tiles and markers without the legacy .leaflet-container class used by the QA.
observations.evidence: Targeted public observation found .map-results-experience=1, 25 .leaflet-tile nodes and 7 marker nodes while .leaflet-container=0.

observations.observation: Clicking the inner marker span or an arbitrary first marker can be intercepted by the mobile close or search-area control.
observations.evidence: Playwright reported pointer interception by .map-mobile-close and .map-search-area during the previous QA implementation.

hypotheses.mechanism: The maps are absent from the product.
hypotheses.prediction: No map button, map experience, tiles or markers will exist after privacy choice and map activation.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Persist essential-only consent, activate the map and inspect its DOM and computed styles.
hypotheses.result: Rejected: the map control became visible and the public map rendered tiles and markers.

hypotheses.mechanism: The QA checks interaction state in the wrong order and targets obsolete or geometrically covered elements.
hypotheses.prediction: Closing first-visit consent, observing .listing-map and selecting a topmost marker wrapper will remove the missing-map and pointer-interception false positives.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Run the corrected public core QA across mobile and low-height map families.
hypotheses.result: Supported: all five mobile map families passed; four of five low-height families passed, with the remaining vacation case isolated from the original missing-toggle failure.

fix.change: The QA now verifies and persists essential-only consent before other journeys, recognizes .listing-map plus real tiles, expands clusters when needed and clicks a topmost marker wrapper by viewport coordinates.
fix.evidence: The focused QA contract suite passed 4 of 4 checks. Public rerun qa-reports/safe-repairs-public-rerun-20261024/comprehensive-1792808296418.json passed all five mobile map families and improved the overall core result from 27/42 to 32/42.

affected_family: Desktop, mobile and low-height interaction viewports

regression_checks.check: First-visit privacy choice is explicitly tested and persists essential-only state.
All five mobile map families open, render and select a map result on public production.

remaining_unknowns: Desktop map cases still exceed the 30-second journey budget and remain a real performance or rendering investigation; this repair does not classify them as healthy.
The low-height vacation map still lacks a pointer-accessible non-cluster marker after the initial cluster expansion and remains open.
authorization_boundary: Repair deterministic QA false positives and verify public read-only behavior; do not publish product changes or relax a genuine performance failure.
